tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessment Year 2018-19: An Appeal withdrawn by opting for settlement of dispute under DTVSV Scheme 2024.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle 7(1), Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: The company has opted for Direct Tax Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme, 2024 for the Assessment Year 2018-19 and filed Form 1 declaration dated 29.01.2025 on e-portal. Accepting application of Company, Form 4 has been issued by Hon'able Pr. CIT on 3rd April 2025. We have discharged additional Income tax liability as on 09.06.2025 as a secondary adjustment pursuant to adjustments u/s 92CA(3). The DTVSV tax refund of Rs.82,99,760/- due to the company for the AY 2018-19 has been wrongly adjusted against the demand liability of AY 2014-15 vide challan no.42874 dtd.31.12.2025. The company has filed rectification letter on 27.02.2026 to arrive at correct position of refund for the year under consideration.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company received notice dated 30-03-2025 u/s 148A for reopening of assessment u/s 147 for AY 2019-20.Subsequently, the Company received further notice dated 06-06-2026 u/s 142(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for the same assesment year.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle
tax_litigation.status: On 15.04.2025 company uploaded its objection for reopening. We believed that since there is no escapement of income, assessment could not be reopened. However, the JAO has ordered the reopening of assessement. The company has filed entire submission to the notice u/s 142(1) of the Act on 07.07.2026

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The company has received show cause notice for proceedings u/s 148A of the income tax act dtd.31.03.2026 for the AY 2020-21.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle
tax_litigation.status: The company has replied to the notice u/s 148A of the act on 06.04.2026.On 09-06-2026, AO has passed order u/s 148A(3) for reopening the assessment on the grounds that deduction u/s 80G with respect to CSR-funded donations amounting to Rs.1,02,50,000/- wrongly allowed in the assessment.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessment Year 2024-25:Assessment proceedings concluded and final order u/s 143(3) of the Income tax Act received on 14-03-2026.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle 7(1), Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: There is an addition of Rs.1.50 lakhs in the final assessment order. However, the Assessing officer has erred in passing order by not allowing certain legitimates deductions. Due to which wrong demand of Rs.23,50,980/- has been outstanding on IT portal. The rectification has been filed by the company on 18.03.2026.The Rectification order u/s 154 of the Income‑tax Act, 1961 was passed on 13.08.2026 and communicated on 08.09.2026, rectified in accordance with the company’s contentions allowing the deductions which was earlier erred in demand computation sheet. However, assessing officer has raised penalty demand of Rs.1,04,832/- u/s 270A of the Income Tax Act,1961.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Company has compiled data yearwise by tagging appropriate lower deduction certificates against demand raised due to shortfall in TDS deduction as well as done required rectifications on traces portal to delete demand raised on account of Inoperative PAN of the employees.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income Tax Officer, TDS Circle 1(1), Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: The notice has been received dtd.03.09.2026 for outstanding demand on Traces Portal. An adjournment has been taken for modifications and corrections on traces portal vide letter dtd.11.09.2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The refund application was rejected by The Asst. Commissioner of CGST. Subsequently an Appeal was filed before Commissioner (Appeals-II) Mumbai against rejection order. The appellate authority upheld the order passed by the Asst. Commissioner of CGST and dismissed the appeal vide O-I-A No. 474/VKP/ADC/APPEALS-II/ME/24-25 Dated 27/02/2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Assistant Commissioner, Central Excise & Central GST, Division VII, Mumbai East Commissionerate
tax_litigation.status: The Writ Petition has filed before Hon'ble Bombay High Court and the next date of hearing is scheduled for 26th Oct, 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Rebate applications rejected by The Asst. Commissioner, Rebate, O-I-O is upheld by Commissioner (Appeals), Mumbai, and The Principal Commissioner & Ex. Officio, Additional Secretary, The Govt., of India, Revisional Authority.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Union of India & Others
tax_litigation.status: Writ Petition filed before Hon'ble Bombay High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Additional Commissioner of Central Excise, Raigad, issued Show Cause cum-demand Notices to recover sanctioned rebate. These demands were confirmed by The Joint Commissioner but subsequently set aside by the Commissioner (Appeals). Thereafter Dept. filed Revision Application to the RA Authority (GOI) which upheld the demand raised in the original Cause cum -demand Notices issued by Additional Commissioner.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Union of India & Others
tax_litigation.status: Writ Petition filed before Hon'ble Bombay High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Deputy Commissioner, C. E. rejected refund application, after which Commissioner (Appeals) and CESTAT also upheld order issued by Dy. Commissioner.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Union of India & Others
tax_litigation.status: Writ Petition filed before Hon'ble Bombay High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Joint Commissioner of CGST and Central Excise, Mumbai East, Mumbai has issued Show Cause Notice with regards to availing IGST Refund on exports in contravention of Rule 96(10) of the CGST Rules, 2017 during FY 2018-19.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner of CGST and Central Excise, Mumbai East, Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld the Judgement of Bomby High Court wherein Hon'ble Bombay High Court had held that all the proceedings in respect of Omission of Rule 96(10) shall stand dispossed off and the said judgement of Hon,ble Supreme Court has been accepted by CBIC by issuing Office Menorandum dated 24th Aug 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Joint Commissioner of CGST and Central Excise, Mumbai East, Mumbai has issued Show Cause Notice with regards to availing IGST Refund on exports in contravention of Rule 96(10) of the CGST Rules, 2017 during the FY 2019-20 to 2023-24.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner of CGST and Central Excise, Mumbai East, Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld the Judgement of Bomby High Court wherein Hon'ble Bombay High Court had held that all the proceedings in respect of Omission of Rule 96(10) shall stand dispossed off and the said judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court has been accepted by CBIC by issuing Office Memorandum dated 24th Aug 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Asst. Commissioner of State Tax, Mazgaon, Mumbai has issued Summons to appear along with details of; i. Payment realization details (FIRC, BRC) of export invoices for which refund had been claimed for the F.Y. 2023-24 & 2024-25. ii. ITC register (Annexure-B) in respect of refund claimed for the F.Y. 2023-24 & 2024-25. iii. Sample copy of export invoices and purchase invoices.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Asst. Commissioner of State Tax, Mazgaon, Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: We appeared before Asst. Commissioner of State Tax and submitted required documents, awaiting for further proceedings / Order.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: GST Jurisdictional Authorities, Vadodara issued Return discrepancy Notice in Form GST ASMT-10 for FY 2022-23. As per Notice, we have availed excess ITC in Form GSTR3B than the same available as per Form GSTR2B for the same tax period.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Superintendent of CGST, Range:I, Div:VII, Vadodara-I Commissionerate
tax_litigation.status: We have filed reply in Form GST ASMT-11 to the subject Notice and are in receipt of closure order in Form GST ASMT-12.

timeline.summary: On 12 May 2026 Bliss GVS Pharma reported postal ballot results: shareholders passed both special resolutions appointing Vijayanarayanan Mahadevan and Deepak Rameshchandra Shah as Non-Executive Independent Directors for five years, with 99.72% of votes polled in favour.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹256.99 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹35.58 Cr.
On 23 May 2026, Bliss GVS Pharma announced an open offer by Anupam Rasayan India Limited following a 43.30% promoter stake purchase agreement at ₹299 per share.
On 2 June 2026 Bliss GVS Pharma said its Palghar (East), Maharashtra manufacturing facility received a WHO Geneva Inspection Closure Report confirming WHO-GMP compliance.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹313.37 Cr (+28.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹52.25 Cr (+91.7% YoY).
